import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define file paths for source data
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_1.csv"
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load Source 0: user ratings data
    # Schema: ['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
    df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)

    # Load Source 1: movie metadata
    # Schema includes ['item_id', 'movie title', ...]
    df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)

    # We want to produce Target1_42 with schema:
    # ['user_id': int, 'item_id': int, 'rating': int, 'timestamp': int, 'movie title': string]

    # Step 1: Join Source0 and Source1 on 'item_id' to get movie titles for each rating
    # Source0 has 50,000 rows, Source1 has 1,682 rows
    # Use inner join to keep only ratings with known movie titles
    df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1[['item_id', 'movie title']], on='item_id', how='inner')

    # Step 2: Ensure data types match target schema
    df_merged['user_id'] = df_merged['user_id'].astype(int)
    df_merged['item_id'] = df_merged['item_id'].astype(int)
    df_merged['rating'] = df_merged['rating'].astype(int)
    df_merged['timestamp'] = df_merged['timestamp'].astype(int)
    df_merged['movie title'] = df_merged['movie title'].astype(str)

    # Step 3: Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
    df_target = df_merged[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]

    # Step 4: Write the transformed data to the target CSV file
    df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
